mcqs.question: Metal A reacts vigorously with cold water producing hydrogen gas, whereas Metal B shows no visible reaction with cold water. Which statement correctly compares their reactivity with water?

options.A: Metal A is less reactive than Metal B because it reacts faster.
options.B: Metal A is more reactive than Metal B because it reacts with cold water while Metal B does not.
options.C: Both metals have the same reactivity; only the temperature of water matters.
options.D: Metal B is more reactive because it does not react with water.

mcqs.answer: Metal A is more reactive than Metal B because it reacts with cold water while Metal B does not.
mcqs.explanation: Metals that react with cold water (e.g., Na, K) are higher in the reactivity series than those that do not react (e.g., Fe, Cu). Therefore, Metal A is more reactive than Metal B. Options A, C and D misinterpret the relationship between reactivity and observed reaction.

mcqs.question: Riya places two metal strips, X and Y, in separate test tubes containing dilute hydrochloric acid. Metal X produces bubbles of hydrogen gas, while Metal Y shows no reaction. Which conclusion best explains this observation?

options.A: Metal X is less reactive than Metal Y because it reacts with acid.
options.B: Metal X is more reactive than Metal Y because it can displace hydrogen from the acid.
options.C: Both metals are equally reactive; the acid concentration is insufficient for Metal Y.
options.D: Metal Y is more reactive because it does not produce hydrogen gas.

mcqs.answer: Metal X is more reactive than Metal Y because it can displace hydrogen from the acid.
mcqs.explanation: In the reactivity series, metals above hydrogen (e.g., Zn, Fe) react with dilute acids to liberate H₂, whereas metals below hydrogen (e.g., Cu, Ag) do not. Hence Metal X must be higher (more reactive) than Metal Y. Options A, C and D contradict the reactivity‑series principle.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is a common misconception about hydrogen displacement reactions?

options.A: Only metals that are higher than hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from acids.
options.B: All metals, regardless of their position in the reactivity series, can displace hydrogen from acids.
options.C: A metal can displace a less reactive metal from its compound solution.
options.D: The reactivity series helps predict whether a metal will evolve hydrogen when reacting with acid.

mcqs.answer: All metals, regardless of their position in the reactivity series, can displace hydrogen from acids.
mcqs.explanation: Statement B is false; only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series (e.g., Zn, Fe) can displace hydrogen. Statements A, C and D correctly describe the concept of hydrogen displacement and the role of the reactivity series.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: According to the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Ni > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au), which metal will NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
mcqs.explanation: Copper lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Zinc, Iron, and Magnesium are above hydrogen and will react, producing hydrogen gas.

mcqs.question: Arrange the following metals in order of decreasing reactivity with water: Sodium (Na), Magnesium (Mg), Aluminium (Al). Which sequence is correct?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium reacts vigorously with cold water, Magnesium reacts slowly with hot water, and Aluminium is protected by a passive oxide layer and shows little reaction. Hence the decreasing order is Na > Mg > Al. The other options misplace the relative reactivities.

mcqs.question: Which metal will evolve hydrogen gas when it reacts with dilute HCl but will NOT react with water at room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc does not react with cold water but reacts with dilute acids to liberate hydrogen, fitting the description. Potassium, Sodium, and Calcium react with water (cold or hot), so they do not satisfy the condition.

mcqs.question: What is meant by a hydrogen displacement reaction in the context of metal reactivity?

options.A: A metal reacts with water to produce oxygen gas.
options.B: A metal higher than hydrogen in the reactivity series displaces hydrogen from an acid.
options.C: Hydrogen gas reacts with a metal to form a metal hydride.
options.D: A metal lower than hydrogen in the series displaces hydrogen from water.

mcqs.answer: A metal higher than hydrogen in the reactivity series displaces hydrogen from an acid.
mcqs.explanation: Hydrogen displacement occurs when a metal situated above hydrogen in the reactivity series reacts with an acid, releasing hydrogen gas. Options A, C, and D describe unrelated processes.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: Will zinc placed in a solution of iron(II) sulfate (FeSO₄) cause any observable reaction?

options.A: Yes, zinc will displace iron, forming zinc sulfate and depositing iron metal.
options.B: No, zinc is less reactive than iron and cannot displace it.
options.C: Yes, but only if the solution is heated.
options.D: No, because both metals are below hydrogen in the series.

mcqs.answer: Yes, zinc will displace iron, forming zinc sulfate and depositing iron metal.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is above iron in the reactivity series, so it can displace iron from its salt solution, producing ZnSO₄ and solid Fe. Options B, C, and D are incorrect based on the series positions.
